## Natural history notes

A small native hornwort characterized by a flat, dark green thallus that forms low rosettes on moist soil and produces slender, upright horn-like sporophytes that emerge from the thallus surface. Carolina Hornwort typically occurs in damp, disturbed habitats such as streambanks, wet fields, ditches, pond margins, and seasonally moist bare soils. It is often most noticeable during wetter periods, when the thallus actively grows and produces spores. Like other hornworts, it lacks true roots, stems, and leaves and contributes to soil stabilization and moisture retention within the microscopic ground-layer community.
